benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
benchmarks.paper_title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
benchmarks.measures: End-to-end terminal task completion by an agent, including environment interaction and verification.
benchmarks.limitations: Agent scaffold, sandbox resources, network access, time limits and model all affect success. A prompt-only score is not Terminal-Bench.
benchmarks.protocol: Harbor + Terminus 2; official task containers and binary final-state verifiers. Report per-task trials and errors; repeated trials are separate from retrying infrastructure failures.
benchmarks.status: Measured pilot: 3 native tasks per model, one trial; full 89-task evaluation not run.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
benchmarks.measures: Python function synthesis from a signature and docstring, checked by execution tests.
benchmarks.limitations: Small public tasks may be contaminated or saturated; test passing does not prove secure or maintainable software.
benchmarks.protocol: Use original completion prompts and hidden tests. Execute generated code in disposable containers. With one completion per task report pass@1 only; chat wrappers must be disclosed.
benchmarks.status: Measured pilot: 10 preselected tasks per model, one completion; not a full benchmark score.

benchmarks.name: MBPP
benchmarks.paper_title: Program Synthesis with Large Language Models
benchmarks.measures: Short Python programs from natural-language specifications.
benchmarks.limitations: Basic programming coverage and sparse tests; original and sanitized subsets are different benchmarks. Public tests can invite overfitting.
benchmarks.protocol: Original test IDs 11–510; keep IDs 2, 3, 4 as three-shot demonstrations for paper-style prompting. Official supplied tests are part of that prompt protocol. Record any zero-shot adaptation separately.
benchmarks.status: Measured pilot: 10 preselected tasks per model, one completion; not a full benchmark score.

benchmarks.name: GSM8K
benchmarks.paper_title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
benchmarks.measures: Multi-step grade-school arithmetic expressed in word problems.
benchmarks.limitations: Answer accuracy does not validate every reasoning step. Widely published questions create contamination risk; not a general reasoning ranking.
benchmarks.protocol: Test split only; fixed prompt and numeric answer extraction after the final #### marker. Disclose examples, reasoning settings and extraction failures. Do not use a learned verifier unless labeled as a different protocol.
benchmarks.status: Measured pilot: 10 preselected tasks per model, one completion; not a full benchmark score.

benchmarks.name: IFEval
benchmarks.paper_title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
benchmarks.measures: Compliance with objectively checkable instructions such as word counts, keywords and formatting.
benchmarks.limitations: Constraint compliance does not establish factual truth, helpfulness or safety. Checker dependencies and strict/loose variants affect scores.
benchmarks.protocol: Retain official prompts, instruction IDs and kwargs; use upstream checkers. Report strict and loose scores separately at both prompt and instruction level.
benchmarks.status: Measured pilot: 10 preselected tasks per model, one completion; not a full benchmark score.
